🎙
News conference by Russia’s G20 Sherpa
Denis Agafonov
following the
third Sherpa meeting
on preparations for the G20 Summit
(Washington, D.C., October 2, 2026)
Key points:
• A series of events, expert meetings and ministerial industry dialogues were held ahead of the G20 Summit in Miami scheduled for December 2026.
• Largely based on the agreements reached during the industry dialogue by the United States, a draft declaration has been developed that will likely be called the Doral Declaration, as custom has it.
• Our meeting focused mainly on the work on this declaration. The discussion helped identify both converging views and areas of disagreement.
• Before the summit convenes, both the presiding party and the sherpas are to find ways to reach consensus and agree on the matters that the country leaders could approve in December in Miami.
• We support the United States’ ambition to produce a finalised and approved document.
• I believe that right now, we are moving in the right direction towards a final declaration that will reflect the actual key economic problems and potential solutions.
#Agenda
• We share the United States’ view that the Group of Twenty shall return to its origins and focus on macroeconomic issues. Our positions are close on many industry-specific topics as well as on energy. However, there are certain matters that should certainly be considered in a slightly different light.
#Geopolitics
• Of course, the geopolitical context occasionally arises in the discussion and it currently has a broad geography, but overall, the dialogue is well-balanced and non-confrontational.
#RussiaG20
• On Russia’s Side, the heads of federal executive bodies at the ministerial level participated in almost all the events concerning the four priorities, which reaffirms our attention and our understanding of the importance of the G20 format.
• The business aspect of Russia-US cooperation within the Group of Twenty can be described as currently being on pause.
• The decision on Russian President Vladimir Putin’s participation in this year’s G20 Summit in Miami will be made closer to the event.
• Russia intends to participate in the G20 events in Britain in 2027.
#SouthAfrica
• The decision [not to invite South Africa to the G20 Summit] is without authority. We insist on South Africa’s immediate reinstatement.
• During
the recent BRICS summit
, participants adopted
the New Delhi Declaration
, which contains a specific paragraph <...> on interaction within the Group of Twenty and clearly articulates the stance of all
#BRICS
countries on solidarity with South Africa.
• We hope that common sense will prevail and South Africa will participate in further events.
#Poland
• US officials have spoken of Poland’s potential participation in the G20. <...> This matter requires the consensus of all G20 countries.
#AI
• The G20, being a framework that consolidates various points of view, could be an appropriate platform for discussing artificial intelligence.

item.title: 🇱🇸 #AmbassadorAmbarov Warmest congratulations to the Kingdom of Lesotho on Independence Day!
item.description: #AmbassadorAmbarov 🇱🇸 🇷🇺 Warmest congratulations to the Kingdom of Lesotho on Independence Day! We extend our heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the Government and the people of Lesotho as the country celebrates the 60th anniversary of its independence . The history of Lesotho’s independence is a testament to the enduring value of self-determination freedom, and sovereignty. 🌐 🤝 Over the decades, diplomatic relations between Russia and Lesotho have been built on a solid foundation of mutual respect and equal partnership . Today, our countries maintain close cooperation within the United Nations and other international platforms, sharing common approaches to global challenges . An important part of our friendship lies in education and humanitarian ties. Since the Soviet era, many Basotho nationals have graduated from Russian universities, and we look forward to continuing this educational exchange for the benefit of both nations. ✨ We wish the people of Lesotho peace, progress and prosperity. May the cooperation between Russia and Lesotho continue to grow stronger! Check out Russian Ambassador Roman Ambarov's congratulatory message published in in Public Eye #RussiaLesotho

🚀
On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union opened humanity’s path to the stars!
#OTD
,
the Space Age officially began
: the world’s first artificial satellite –
Sputnik 1
– entered Earth’s orbit.
At 10:28 pm Moscow time
, an
R-7 launch vehicle
, developed under the leadership of the outstanding Soviet rocket engineer
Sergey Korolev
, lifted off from the Tyuratam launch site (later named
Baikonur
). Just over five minutes later, the satellite separated from the rocket and transmitted its world-famous signals:
“Beep! Beep!”
📰
On October 5, 1957,
Soviet newspaper Pravda
reported
:
On October 4, 1957, the USSR successfully launched the first satellite.
The satellite is currently following an elliptical orbit around Earth, and its flight can be observed in the light of the rising and setting Sun using the simplest optical instruments.
Updates on the movement of the first artificial satellite, launched in the USSR on October 4, will be broadcast regularly by radio stations.
🛰
An aluminium sphere 58 centimetres
(~23 inches)
in diameter, weighing 83.6 kilograms
(~184 pounds)
, with four antennas and two radio transmitters
– this was humanity’s first envoy in orbit. Behind its simple exterior lay the immense efforts of Soviet scientists, engineers and workers.
Sputnik completed an orbit around Earth roughly every 96 minutes
, and radio enthusiasts worldwide picked up its famous signals.
Its radio transmitters operated for about three weeks, while the satellite itself remained in orbit for 92 days
. During that time, it completed
1,440 orbits around Earth
, travelling
some 60 million kilometres
(~ 37.3 million miles). Its flight ended on
January 4, 1958
, when it entered the dense layers of the atmosphere and burned up.
The historic launch validated the calculations and technical solutions needed to reach space
. Observations of the satellite gave scientists new data on the density of the upper atmosphere and the propagation of radio waves through the ionosphere.
🌐
Sputnik 1 was a triumph of Soviet science and engineering – an achievement for all humanity.
It proved that the path beyond Earth was open – paving the way for
Yuri Gagarin’s flight
, the exploration of the Moon and other planets, and the construction of orbital stations.
For
6️⃣
9️⃣
years, satellites have served humanity.
Today, they are essential to everyday life: they provide communications and television broadcasting, help us navigate, forecast the weather and monitor climate change.
☝️
But the first was ours. Forever.
#Sputnik1

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 2, the Russian Foreign Ministry hosted the opening of an exhibition of archival documents and photographs marking the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇧🇳 On October 2, the Russian Foreign Ministry hosted the opening of an exhibition of archival documents and photographs marking the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Russia and Brunei . In their welcoming remarks, Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko and Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Brunei Darussalam to Russia Husaini Alauddin reaffirmed their countries’ commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation in a spirit of friendship, trust and mutual respect . The Sides expressed their determination to expand political dialogue and deepen ties in defence and security, trade and humanitarian exchanges. They also noted that Russia and Brunei share identical or similar positions on key international and regional issues . The event was also attended by Heads of diplomatic missions of other #ASEAN member states in Moscow, representatives of Russian ministries and agencies, civil society and academia, and journalists. #RussiaBrunei

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a media question
regarding the withdrawal of foreign troops from Iraq
(October 2, 2026)
❓
Question: On September 30, the US-led Anti-ISIS Coalition announced the completion of its troop withdrawal from Iraq. How does Russia view this event?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
Indeed, on September 30,
the twelve-year presence in Iraq of the so-called International Anti-ISIS Coalition came to an end.
All remaining bases of the US Armed Forces and their allies in the country – mainly within Iraqi Kurdistan – have been fully transferred to the control of the Iraqi military.
The decision by the Iraqi Parliament, adopted in January 2020 and fully
reflecting the aspiration of its people to restore and consolidate state sovereignty
after the prolonged presence of foreign forces, has thus been implemented.
That presence had effectively continued since 2003 – from the moment of the American invasion under a completely contrived pretext, which triggered decades of instability across the wider region.
The withdrawal of troops from Iraq, which
we certainly welcome
, demonstrates that the Iraqi army and security forces are capable of independently addressing the task of strengthening the state’s defence capability and ensuring national security. They are capable, among other things, of countering the terrorist threat emanating from ISIS and other such organisations.
We are convinced that
the Iraqi people will be able to successfully withstand any internal and external challenges that confront them.
The guarantee of this lies in neighbourly relations and coordination with neighbouring countries; in this regard, we would like once again to draw attention to
the Collective Security Concept for the Gulf Region proposed by Russia.
☝️
It proceeds from the understanding that it is precisely the states located there, such as Iraq, that
play the leading role in maintaining stability in this strategically important region through close interaction among themselves.

Vienna, September 30, 2026
Agenda item: Special Military operation to demilitarize and denazify Ukraine
• The reckless actions of the Kiev regime's Western sponsors continue to pose a threat to peace and security. Right now, Europe is
doing everything it can to hinder a peaceful settlement and disrupt the prospects for negotiations
: they are pumping the Ukrainian regime with money and weapons, and helping to aim UAVs and missiles at civilians and civilian infrastructure.
• European countries are deliberately escalating the situation.
They continue to convince their citizens of a mythical "Russian threat" and the need to prepare for hostilities, for a war against Russia
. Their goal is
the routinization and normalization of a critical scenario in the public consciousness
. The course toward fueling the conflict is evident.
• It has long been clear that the territory of Ukraine is being used by
#NATO
member states as
a testing ground for trying out new weapons systems and disposing of old ones under real combat conditions
. However, it is also a convenient way for Western pseudo-peacemakers to fight Russia by proxy for the time being, while remaining "above the main fray." To this end, the process of "merging" the military-industrial complexes of Ukraine and European countries is underway at full speed.
• The current course of European governments is clearly aimed at
preparing their military-industrial complex, state apparatus, economy, and civilian infrastructure for aggressive actions against Russia
. Under these conditions, the recent statements made in New York by
#NATO
Secretary General M. Rutte—that
#NATO
countries are ready to provide Ukraine with certain security guarantees after the conflict—prove once again that
neither the Kiev regime nor its Western handlers are aimed at de-escalation and a settlement
.
• Within the framework of the special military operation, we note numerous instances of the Kiev regime violating the norms and principles of international humanitarian law (IHL). Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) units are mining territories of the Russian Federation to inflict damage on
civilian infrastructure and the peaceful population
. To this end, Kiev deliberately uses mines, booby traps, and improvised explosive devices, which are deployed to mine roadsides between settlements, bridges, dams, residential buildings, medical institutions, schools, and kindergartens.
• In the European Union, where they boast of "European values," they have remained completely silent: not a single word of condemnation.
They only say that Ukraine is helping to defend "European values."
In the West, humanitarian norms are being transformed from universal obligations into a tool for selective polemics, while the interests of the victims recede into the background, if not the third plan.
• The West also covers up
widespread human rights violations during mobilization in Ukraine
. This refers to the forced delivery of citizens to territorial recruitment centers (TRCs), unlawful imprisonment, physical violence, and the obstruction of access to legal assistance.
• Having started the special military operation in 2022 to protect the people of Donbas and Novorossiya from extermination by the Kiev regime, Russia continues to fight for their security and rights in full accordance with the letter and spirit of the UN Charter.
Our struggle for truth and justice will be carried through to the end: the goals of the SMO will be achieved, threats to Russia's security eliminated, and peaceful life restored
.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On 1 October Russian Ambassador to India Denis Alipov took part in the ceremony at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandi.
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇮🇳 On 1 October Russian Ambassador to India Denis Alipov took part in the ceremony at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandi. 🖼️ As part of the event the Ambassador together with the Head of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi Shri Pravesh Wahi inaugurated the “Tolstoy–Gandhi” exhibition, prepared by the Russian Embassy. The exhibition features copies of letters exchanged between the two great thinkers and reflect their philosophical ideas and intellectual dialogue. 🎙️ In his remarks the Ambassador stressed that the shared philosophical legacy of Leo Tolstoy and Mahatma Gandhi continues to serve as a bridge between Russia and India. He also noted that the exhibition demonstrates the influence of the great Russian writer’s ideas on the intellectual development of the leader of India’s national liberation movement. 🤝 Among those attending the opening were Alexander Dodonov , Head of the Russian House in Delhi, representatives of official circles and the diplomatic corps, municipal officials and journalists. 💬 The official program was followed by the active discussion. #DruzhbaDosti #RussiaIndia #MahatmaGhandi #LeoTolstoy

On 1 October Russian Ambassador to India
Denis Alipov
took part in the ceremony at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandi.
🖼️
As part of the event the Ambassador together with the Head of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi
Shri Pravesh Wahi
inaugurated the “Tolstoy–Gandhi” exhibition, prepared by the Russian Embassy. The exhibition features copies of letters exchanged between the two great thinkers and reflect their philosophical ideas and intellectual dialogue.
🎙️
In his remarks the Ambassador stressed that the shared philosophical legacy of Leo Tolstoy and Mahatma Gandhi continues to serve as a bridge between Russia and India. He also noted that the exhibition demonstrates the influence of the great Russian writer’s ideas on the intellectual development of the leader of India’s national liberation movement.
🤝
Among those attending the opening were
Alexander Dodonov
, Head of the Russian House in Delhi, representatives of official circles and the diplomatic corps, municipal officials and journalists.
💬
The official program was followed by the active discussion.
